data.narrative:
Anduril Industries, a Series H defense and security company founded by Palmer Luckey, Brian Schimpf, Trae Stephens, Matt Grimm, and Joe Chen, is valued at $61B following $11B+ in total capital raised. The valuation is assessed against a comparable universe of 10 companies—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers—operating in the same sector and valuation tier.

The peer-median method applied here uses three same-sector comparables: Helsing (Series E, $18.0B), Castelion (Series C, $13.0B), and Shield AI (Series G, $12.7B). The median valuation across this peer set is $13.0B, with a range spanning $12.7B to $18.0B. This method is the primary triangulation input available given data constraints.

The triangulated valuation range is $11.1B (low) to $14.9B (high), with a median of $13.0B. This analysis rests on a single methodological pillar, creating material constraint on confidence. The current $61B valuation sits substantially above the peer-referenced range, reflecting either a significant stage premium for Series H capital, material divergence in growth or margin profile relative to peers, or market repricing since the last comparable data point. Key uncertainties include whether peer valuations reflect recent market conditions and whether Anduril's revenue, growth rate, or strategic position warrant a valuation multiple significantly above the median peer set.
